Each proposed source is a candidate only. The current quest, press, and event owners must expose a fact that can be translated into an evidence event. No UI choice calls `RecordEvidence` directly with a hand-authored positive or negative value.

### Field 02 expansion — Canonical dimension crosswalk and prohibited shortcuts

| Reputation dimension | Public-works situation that may become evidence | Required owner fact before any evidence is recorded | Prohibited shortcut |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reliability | A stated scope or delivery date was honored, revised, or abandoned | Project/quest owner returns the actual commitment and result | “Player chose a responsible option” |
| Strength | A perimeter-facing repair is verified and communicated | Current defense/build owner confirms the change and evidence reaches an audience | “Wall looks stronger in the scene” |
| Generosity | A shared service or material aid is accepted by its recipient | Inventory/service owner confirms transfer and recipient result | “Clinic was mentioned in dialogue” |
| Ruthlessness | A contested safety decision has a real, owner-recorded coercive outcome | Combat/governance/quest owner exposes the supported consequence | “The player refused a project” |
| Wealth | Trade-facing abundance or shortage becomes public knowledge | Trade/production owner confirms the fact and a supported medium carries it | “A project used rare material” |

This matrix is an authoring review aid, not a new rule table for reputation scoring. The five dimensions can move in a direction that surprises the player or results in no evidence at all. The reputation owner’s current ranges, evidence multipliers, tag thresholds, decay, and trade-price projection remain authoritative. No civic plan adds its own “trust,” “accountability,” “repair quality,” or “project fame” score.

### Field 03 expansion — Evidence-source cards with unique, reviewable identity

Each candidate evidence card declares the source event ID pattern, owner event that proves it, reputation dimension under consideration, information medium, intended audience if any, exact observable text, duplicate-prevention expectation, and fallback if the owner result is absent. Source IDs must identify a real underlying event rather than a chapter title. A print run and its later rumor can be separate evidence events only if both are accepted by their owners and they represent materially distinct facts; replaying the same project page must not create a second evidence entry.

The authoring review marks each candidate `EVIDENCE-READY`, `DIALOGUE-ONLY`, or `HELD`. `EVIDENCE-READY` requires an owner event and a live seam into reputation recording. `DIALOGUE-ONLY` means residents may hold conflicting views but no numerical reputation is asserted. `HELD` means the proposed action, medium, or audience has not been verified. This classification prevents content volume from creating false claims about system reachability.

### Field 04 expansion — Storyline: The Work Everyone Heard About

An outpost asks for a path repair before a public gathering. The project owner accepts a limited inspection but not a construction job. One faction sends a message saying the shelter has promised more than it can deliver. A public notice is prepared with the exact accepted scope, limitations, and review date. The press owner may accept, refuse, or price the run. Later, the project owner returns whether the inspection occurred; the event may qualify for a candidate reliability fact only if a real, stable outcome is emitted and the reputation owner has an approved interpretation.

In the second act, an unrelated delay changes how the residents describe the promise. The player can publish a correction, preserve the original notice beside the correction, or leave the account unchanged. The story presents trade reactions only if the current reputation/trade projection changes and the owning trade system consumes it. The ending reports the delivered work and the public claim separately. It can be emotionally satisfying even when no reputation evidence is recorded, because the player chose how accurately to communicate an imperfect result.

### Field 05 expansion — Side quest deck: audience, evidence, and consequence

**A Notice at the Gate** asks whether a draft names the accepted scope. Completion evidence is a successful print result, not the existence of copy. **Who Took the Bricks?** compares a production batch, inventory movement, and recipient result; only the relevant owner confirms custody. **The Third Account** records witness disagreement without selecting the version that best serves the player. **A Contract Kept Small** lets the player narrow an overpromised work request through its real owner, if amendment exists. **One Receipt for Two Markets** explores the difference between a witnessed handoff and trader word; the same source cannot be scored twice through two media unless the reputation owner considers them distinct events. **The Apology on the Notice Board** can publish a correction, but it cannot remove a prior reputation record or guarantee restored trust.

Each side quest declares its supported closure: action accepted, action refused, fact verified, no source found, or narrative-only disagreement preserved. A quest that culminates in a correction can still leave the earlier claim visible. No “clean record” button hides public history, and no reward grants free trade discounts.

### Field 06 expansion — Reputation feedback without manipulative reward loops

If a candidate project result records evidence, the UI reads the resulting reputation projection from its owner and identifies the underlying event. It does not preview a precise future price change unless the current trade owner can return that quote. It never promises that an audience will respond positively to a correction, and it does not tell the player to repeat low-cost aid actions to farm the Sanctuary tag. Reputation’s own anti-farming check, evidence history, daily decay, derived tags, and trade modifier remain untouched.

Feedback appears after the source event has been accepted and recorded. The player sees the dimension/evidence phrase only when that is the current system’s intended presentation; raw score internals remain optional technical detail. A null return from the anti-duplicate check means no new evidence was added. A panel reopening cannot re-record the original event. A reversed project outcome must be represented by a new fact or owner-supported correction, never by rewriting history locally.

### Field 07 expansion — Work portfolio projection and filter behavior

The proposed public-work portfolio may show a compact “public account” strip for a selected project: verified scope, actual result, audience-facing publication if any, and linked reputation evidence if the reputation owner returns a match. The strip is informational. It does not become an authority for current reputation values or trade prices. Filtering can select “evidence recorded,” “narrative only,” and “source unresolved,” but never a fabricated project score or best/worst community ranking.

The page keeps materials and public perception separate. Kiln quality, quantity transferred, construction acceptance, and maintenance follow-up remain in their current owners. A resident quote can be shown beside a receipt without being promoted to the same confidence class. Empty states explain whether no reputation event occurred, no owner query exists, or the data is currently unknown.

### Field 08 expansion — Accessibility, social safety, and contested accounts

Public disagreement is an authored story outcome, not a red/green reputation puzzle. The player can choose to publish less, refuse to expose a witness, or preserve a correction privately. A single resident’s speech is not shown as a survey of the whole colony. The UI attributes each claim to its source and date, and distinguishes “the engine recorded evidence” from “the public agrees.” Color, faction emblem, or sound alone cannot indicate approval.

Reviewers check that marginalized residents are not made responsible for proving whether the shelter is generous or treacherous; that aid recipients can decline publicity; and that no event treats a truthful account as automatically favorable. Controller navigation reaches evidence details and privacy controls. Audio cues are supplementary and respect audio accessibility preferences. Copy avoids presenting trade price penalties as moral judgments.

### Field 09 expansion — Deduplication, event scale, and archive boundaries

The evidence history can grow across long campaigns. A work portfolio queries only the selected project’s known source IDs if a bounded lookup exists; it must not scan all reputation events for each list row. The content adapter subscribes only while its panel is open and disposes listeners on close or campaign replacement. Reputation tags and prices are fetched as read projections when shown, not recomputed by every project panel.

Every candidate source ID is deterministic and stable for a real owner event. It is not derived from hash iteration order or a random UI key. The reputation owner’s own source ID/media/audience anti-duplicate rule applies. Archive entries remain historical facts and reputation evidence remains an interpretation record; neither stores a duplicate copy of a public-works ledger. On reload, the project owner and reputation owner are queried independently and linked only if the canonical source identifiers still match.

### Field 10 expansion — Integration and acceptance gates

Stage 1 is a read-only research pass: enumerate actual project/press events and test whether any current event already reaches reputation recording. Stage 2 drafts the source crosswalk without mutating scores. Stage 3 selects one verifiable project event and proves exactly one evidence record through the existing owner seam. Stage 4 verifies the resulting dimension/tag/price projections through their current consumers. If no host event exists, the pass ends at Stage 2 and content remains dialogue-only; a new global reputation bridge is an architecture decision, not an assumed convenience.

Acceptance includes honored and missed scopes, accepted/failed print run, correction after the original account, missing or mismatched source event, duplicate panel reopen, multiple media with one event, audience omitted, save/reload, daily decay, tag derivation, and trade quote. The focused verification is selected by the eventual package owner and remains bounded. The release summary reports the exact event IDs and dimension outcomes observed; “civic project reputation integrated” is not claimed from a single unverified content path.

## Pass 34 — Cross-settlement service requests under live territory conditions

This pass expands Common Ground beyond the home shelter by using the newly integrated 12-row settlement catalog and 19-row faction-territory catalog as location and access references. Its purpose is to make a public service request feel grounded in a real community, trade need, allegiance, and current route/control context. It does not create a second settlement catalog, local work-order ledger, civic diplomacy system, or territory map. A settlement may request an inspection or service in authored content; the existing settlement, travel, quest, territory, inventory, construction, and public-works owners decide whether the player can actually act.

### Field 01 expansion — A remote request begins with a canonical place

Each candidate service card is anchored to one `settlement_id` and its canonical `location_id`. `route_node` is a separate catalog reference and is never substituted for a map location without proof that the travel owner accepts it. The request includes the settlement’s current catalog identity, archetype, relevant trade need or export, and the owner(s) that would be required to inspect, travel, transfer material, publish, or complete work. Current population, faction allegiance, and gate data are read from their owners when the player selects a request; no local snapshot is treated as present-day truth.

The first playable loop is request review, not dispatch: open one settlement, read its report, check whether a travel route and current territory result exist, then choose to pursue an already-supported action, send a supported message, or defer. If the game has no command for remote project proposals, the request remains a narrative consultation. A missing command does not cause a new local work-order status.

### Field 02 expansion — Settlement and territory have separate jobs

`SettlementCatalog` describes the community reference, location, archetype, faction relation, goods/needs, keeper/trader/fixture candidates, and a linked sidework quest ID. `TerritoryControlSystem` models faction territories, control points, contested zones, trade tax, travel safety, and dynamic contestation/fortification. Those facts answer different questions. A settlement’s stated attitude does not override current faction standing. A static territory label does not authorize travel. A trade tax is not an additional public-works material cost unless the current trade owner returns that quote.

The service view first queries the current standing/entry rule, then asks the travel owner for a reachable route, then displays the territory result as context. It does not calculate a composite “safe to build” score. If those queries are not exposed in the Godot host, the authoring packet can reference the existing catalog but is not labeled playable. Arrival, local inspection, order acceptance, material transfer, and repair completion are separate receipts.

### Field 03 expansion — Twelve-site intake crosswalk

The initial geography set contains Brine-Pan Hollow (`settlement_brine_pans`, Salt Camp), Iron Siding (`settlement_iron_siding`, Rail Siding Town), Cape Beacon Commune (`settlement_cape_beacon`, Coastal Lighthouse Commune), Slate Hollow (`settlement_slate_hollow`, Quarry Enclave), Pilgrim Hearth (`settlement_pilgrim_hearth`, monastic sanctuary), Tinkers’ Notch (`settlement_tinkers_notch`, free trader scrap market), Ferry Crossing and Nine Rails (trade posts), Fort Karkov and Lock Seven (strongholds), Silo Burrow (refugee camp), and St. Nicholas (religious/ideological community).

For each site, authors create one intake question grounded in its current description or trade need, not an assumed construction request. The question asks who may authorize a visit, what evidence would verify the reported need, which canonical item/route/repair owner could act, whether a linked sidework quest is current, and what a truthful no-action ending says. A card can be marked `REFERENCE_ONLY`, `QUEST_LINK_CANDIDATE`, `TRAVEL_REVIEW_REQUIRED`, or `OWNER_ACTION_VERIFIED`; only the final state supports an operational completion claim.

### Field 04 expansion — Territory posture and contested-zone review

The 19 canonical territories include territorial, nomadic, ideological, and mixed classifications, with control strength, trade tax, travel safety, control points, and declared contestation. A service request can cite the territory and current control result as context for negotiation or logistics. It cannot change ownership because the player delivered supplies. It cannot claim territory transfer from a completed quest unless the territory owner returns that change. Contested zones are especially important: a project card must show the exact current controller/contestation result at the time of action, not a value copied into authored JSON.

The movement sequence is: check settlement entry conditions; request current route and hazard/access status; display relevant territory projection; confirm the supported operation; then refresh each owner after completion. A hostile or unavailable entry response exits cleanly into message, delay, or refusal options where those commands exist. It does not strand the player in a fabricated work phase.

### Field 05 expansion — Storyline: The Measure Between Settlements

Two neighboring settlements submit requests that appear to conflict: one wants a route kept open for trade, another fears that the same access exposes its residents. The player visits or contacts each location only through supported travel/communications. The first community asks for a limited survey; the second asks to see the source record. Territory data shows current control and travel context, while the settlement records show each community’s own goods/needs and faction relation. The player cannot use a catalog description to declare either settlement’s current leader or public mood.

In the middle chapters, the player compares a reported material need with a real inventory or trade quote and a route result. One settlement refuses entry after a standing gate; another accepts a conversation but not an inspection. The player may choose a smaller action, publish a transparent explanation, or close without work. A final chapter records separate receipts: who was reached, which inspection was accepted, what was transferred, whether a work owner completed a task, and what remained blocked. The two settlements are not merged into a new regional council.

### Field 06 expansion — Side quests with local evidence and boundaries

**Salt Against the Rain** asks whether Brine-Pan Hollow can provide a canonical preservative good for a verified request; the trade/inventory owner decides stock and cost. **Destination Still Painted** at Iron Siding asks whether a route notice reflects current map/travel facts; cartography and travel owners confirm the answer. **The Light Is Not a Road** at Cape Beacon asks whether an optics report identifies a hazard or merely a landmark; no safe passage is inferred from a lighthouse. **Measure the Stone** at Slate Hollow checks whether a proposed masonry use matches an actual kiln/building consumer. **A Dry Threshold** at a refugee camp asks for a drainage inspection only if the current water/maintenance owner has a supported command. **The Unfinished Crossing** asks whether a trade-post delivery was accepted; transport and inventory receipts decide closure.

Each quest can end in a verified action, an owner refusal, an access block, a declined invitation, or an unresolved request. The name of a canonical settlement does not make the quest reachable. If its `sidework_quest_id` has no current consumer, the cross-link is held and the main scene remains a request, not an active quest.

### Field 07 expansion — Regional service board UX

The board displays canonical settlement name, local time/day as available, current request status from the owner, current route check, and relevant territory facts with source attribution. It avoids the clutter of loading every NPC, stock list, side quest, territory history, and trade quote on the map at once. Selecting a place fetches details on demand. A map marker is shown only if its canonical location resolves through the map owner; `route_node` remains an internal reference unless the route owner explicitly consumes it.

The player can sort by request urgency only when a real owner returns urgency; otherwise the board sorts alphabetically or by stable catalog ID. Filters for archetype, current access, and territory classification explain that they are navigation aids, not recommendations. Disabled actions include the exact owner reason and an alternate next step, such as “check route,” “request permission,” or “close request.” Keyboard focus and controller back behavior remain predictable when one settlement disappears from a refreshed projection.

### Field 08 expansion — Representation and faction boundaries

Every settlement is a community with internal differences. Its catalog value, allegiance, or threat level cannot be used as a shortcut for individual consent or a stereotype. A stronghold can contain residents who oppose its leader; a religious community can disagree internally; a refugee camp cannot be portrayed as a single grateful voice. The story creates named witnesses only after canonical NPC/voice checks and does not invent new leaders through the catalog display name.

Faction standing, entry permission, territory hostility, and settlement attitude are shown as distinct concepts. The player can respect a refusal and leave without a hidden reputation loss. A trade offer is not a diplomatic treaty. A public notice does not change faction control. The content review ensures that optional routes do not equate aid with compelled allegiance.

### Field 09 expansion — Data scale and owner-call budget

The static index can show twelve settlements without querying all nineteen territories and every quest. Selecting a place resolves one settlement row, its current territory references, one route/standing check, and one request source. Territory history and full trade stock load only after deliberate inspection. The project view stores stable settlement and owner-result references; it does not cache population, attitude, trade tax, route safety, or control strength as mutable project fields.

An acceptance profile opens the regional board repeatedly, runs with all territories contested, removes an optional quest target, changes standing, and loads a long work history. It verifies bounded queries, no per-frame territory scans, no repeated dispatch, and correct cleanup on route failure. Deterministic ordering uses stable IDs. Any dynamic territory result follows TerritoryControlSystem’s save/restore and seeded rules; authored request order cannot advance or perturb it.

### Field 10 expansion — Reachability gates and content-release pack

The initial content pack contains twelve intake cards and six side-quest candidates, but content count does not equal playable count. A row graduates only with a current settlement query, map/location resolution, territory/standing response, route command, task owner, result receipt, and UI route. The evidence sheet names the exact owner for each step and flags where only JSON/catalog presence has been proven. At least one settlement from each proposed archetype grouping must pass the complete route before the regional board is described as operational.

Focused acceptance covers friendly, wary, and hostile access; current and stale territory references; contested/control shift; unavailable route; no standing; absent linked quest; stock shortage; transfer failure; travel success; visit declined; missing location; out-of-date catalog; and save/load at each owner-declared persistence point. If the current host lacks a route, that settlement remains `REFERENCE_ONLY`. The new geography makes public service work regional and politically legible while keeping settlement, territory, standing, travel, inventory, and construction truth with their current authorities.

### Pass 34 supplemental docket — Twenty public-account stories

These story records expand the reputation/evidence axis without introducing a civic score. Each card is tagged with a likely evidence dimension for review, but remains `DIALOGUE-ONLY` until an actual event source reaches the existing reputation owner. The dimension is a hypothesis about public interpretation, not a guaranteed delta.

| Card | Incident | Candidate interpretation | Evidence needed before mechanical effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `civic_scope_kept_01` | Crew completes only the authorized inspection | Reliability | Work owner returns scope and completion receipt |
| `civic_scope_revised_01` | Scope is narrowed after material shortage | Reliability | Accepted amendment and public notice result |
| `civic_date_corrected_01` | Published date is corrected before work begins | Reliability | Press owner confirms correction reached audience |
| `civic_delay_hidden_01` | A delay is omitted from a notice | Reliability | Supported publication plus actual work delay |
| `civic_aid_accepted_01` | Community accepts shared medical supplies | Generosity | Inventory transfer and receiving owner confirmation |
| `civic_aid_declined_01` | Recipient refuses public delivery | Generosity | Transfer owner confirms no handoff; no score by default |
| `civic_food_share_01` | Food is sent with consent to a settlement | Generosity | Canonical item transfer and recipient/source event |
| `civic_private_aid_01` | Aid is delivered without public naming | Generosity | Owner confirms delivery; privacy medium remains private |
| `civic_material_shortage_01` | A public works batch cannot be supplied | Wealth | Production/trade owner returns actual shortage |
| `civic_market_quote_01` | A merchant gives a current price for project materials | Wealth | Trade quote and audience event, if the owner supports it |
| `civic_export_reserved_01` | Export stock is reserved for local repairs | Wealth | Trade/inventory owner confirms reservation and amount |
| `civic_price_disputed_01` | Two factions cite different prices | Wealth | Preserve both quotes; no derived score without accepted evidence |
| `civic_gate_reinforced_01` | A perimeter work scope is actually completed | Strength | Construction/defense owner confirms installed change |
| `civic_gate_unfinished_01` | Work stops before a defensive improvement exists | Strength | Owner returns partial/cancelled result; no completed-work claim |
| `civic_forceful_clearance_01` | Residents report coercive removal for a worksite | Ruthlessness | Governance/quest owner verifies the supported decision |
| `civic_nonviolent_delay_01` | Work pauses to respect a resident’s refusal | Ruthlessness | Usually dialogue-only unless owner records a real choice |
| `civic_witness_account_01` | One witness contradicts a printed work receipt | Unassigned | Preserve provenance; no vote or forced dimension |
| `civic_territory_claim_01` | Two factions dispute who approved a route repair | Unassigned | Current territory/quest result; no campaign-owned control |
| `civic_maintenance_return_01` | A custodian returns to inspect an accepted work | Reliability | Maintenance owner emits the actual follow-up result |
| `civic_archive_correction_01` | An old project record is corrected with a new source | Reliability | Archive/press result; original remains discoverable |

Every card adds four authored fields: `trigger_evidence`, `public_claim`, `private_fact`, and `unresolved_questions`. The public claim contains only what a current owner has verified. The private fact is not automatically shared with traders, factions, or radio. `unresolved_questions` carries dissent forward without converting it into an arbitrary quest failure. The card is playable as a conversation even if there is no reputation event, but its outcome is explicitly nonmechanical.

Before promoting a record, the integrator confirms the exact action owner, current event payload, source ID stability, audience/medium, reputation dimension, accepted scoring authority, and observable readback. Content authors cannot choose delta, confidence, or salience from a table because that would make the public-works plan a second reputation balancer. If no exact source exists, the record stays narrative-only and still supports a meaningful choice about disclosure, scope, or consent.

## Pass 35 — Resident-initiated work and principled refusal

This pass uses the integrated `SurvivorAutonomySystem` as a source of resident-initiated project ideas, help offers, and work refusals. It addresses a gap in many management loops: projects are presented only as player-selected tasks even when current survivors can autonomously initiate a perimeter project, refuse an assignment, express duty preferences, or pursue mastery. The feature is a handoff between the autonomy owner and whatever current construction, roster, inventory, or civic quest owner accepts the action. It is not another project board or volunteer roster.

### Field 01 expansion — Requests can originate with residents

When the autonomy owner emits `initiate_fortify_perimeter`, the community board may receive a project candidate containing only the actor, owner-provided action reference, and any supported context. The player can inspect the proposed work through the current construction/build owner, which decides whether a valid target, cost, schedule, and command exist. If it accepts the request, the existing construction owner creates or updates the project state. If it refuses, the candidate closes with that reason. A prose event cannot create a project by setting a local `initiated=true` flag.

Other action templates can be useful in the work context: `help_relieve_workload`, `help_mentor_skills`, `pursue_mastery_project`, and `express_duty_preference`. These may inform who wants to contribute or what task feels suitable, but each recommendation is a statement of autonomy state, not a qualification or assignment. The current roster/skill/build owner still checks eligibility and capacity. When no owner can accept the suggestion, it remains a conversation and the project continues without a fake contributor.

### Field 02 expansion — Refusal is a first-class project outcome

The autonomy catalog includes `refuse_resentment_work`, `refuse_exhaustion_duty`, `refuse_trauma_danger`, and `refuse_low_morale_drill`. Work requests should use the exact event the engine emits and the current task identity; they must not collapse all refusals into a generic “worker unhappy” state. The player can honor the refusal, inspect whether the current task can be reassigned, reduce scope if the project owner supports amendment, or defer/cancel. A respected refusal should not silently delete the resident’s autonomy goal or lower morale through a plan-local consequence.

If the player chooses an existing explicit override, `OnWorkRefusalOverriddenSeam` and its actual consequence remain with SurvivorAutonomySystem. The confirmation summarizes the exact consequence returned by the owner and names the affected task. There is no generic override button for medical consent, personal memorials, private testimony, or faction identity. The project board cannot reinterpret a refusal as an attendance failure.

### Field 03 expansion — Project intake event contract

The candidate event envelope is a read model with `actor_survivor_id`, `autonomy_action_id`, `target_owner_reference`, `source_event_id`, `emitted_day`, `supported_action_route`, and `current_status`. It omits local worker assignment, project cost, target construction stage, and completion state. The current integration seam may expose only some of these fields; the implementation gate is to use the actual payload rather than expanding the envelope in this plan.

The request identity is stable and idempotent. Opening the card or refreshing the portfolio never runs autonomy again or emits another `OnProjectInitiatedSeam`. A project owner’s accepted command becomes the actual project. A refusal becomes a terminal or review state only if that owner supports it. Otherwise the card stays a transient prompt and the player can dismiss it without writing data.

### Field 04 expansion — Storyline: The Work Nobody Asked For

A resident independently proposes a perimeter repair after a difficult storm season. The player checks whether the current construction owner recognizes the exact structure and whether required materials are available. At the same time, two other residents refuse a hazardous work rotation for different autonomy reasons: one from exhaustion, one because the danger conflicts with a personal boundary. A fourth resident offers to mentor a novice worker. The board presents all four owner events as distinct and asks the player to scope the repair around actual capacity.

In chapter two, one project advocate calls the refusals selfish. An ideological confrontation occurs only if IdeologicalFrictionEvents reaches its own threshold. The player can choose its supported mediation option, potentially broker compromise, stay neutral, or side with one participant. If a conversion or bunker split occurs according to that owner’s rules, the story records the actual outcome but does not treat it as project approval. At the close, the player can accept a smaller construction plan, defer it, or stop; project completion is proved only by the construction owner.

### Field 05 expansion — Side stories and source receipts

**A Wall Started in Conversation** follows the resident’s initiation and ends when construction accepts or refuses the request. **The Shift After Nightfall** uses an exhaustion refusal and asks the roster owner whether work can be changed. **Show Me Before I Sign** lets a novice accept mentoring only after both survivors agree and the skill/roster route supports it. **The Quiet Drill** follows a low-morale drill refusal without interpreting it as sabotage. **Three on One Side** can begin only after the ideology owner reports at least three survivors forming opposing factions; a chapter cannot create that threshold. **No One Needs to Win This Meeting** uses the formal mediation quest only when the current affinity trigger fires.

Each story separates the autonomy event, project command, material transaction, task assignment, and completed construction receipt. These can occur on different days or not at all. “Resident initiated,” “player approved,” “materials transferred,” “builder accepted,” and “work complete” are never collapsed into one success label.

### Field 06 expansion — Ideology is not project arbitration

The integrated ideological events use real thresholds: confrontation at affinity less than or equal to -50, conversion attempt at affinity greater than or equal to 30, bunker-wide schism when at least three survivors form opposing factions, and urgent mediation at affinity less than or equal to -80. The project plan consumes those events only as social context. IdeologicalFrictionEvents decides when they occur and which responses are legal. Construction and project owners decide what may be built.

The project must not add ideology requirements to a build recipe, infer allegiance from a shelter-reputation tag, or use a mediation outcome to overwrite a resident’s work refusal. A compromise may improve a conversation while the project remains unaffordable. A split may make the work-site plan harder to coordinate without changing the already accepted engineering facts. The player sees these as parallel, explicit outcomes.

### Field 07 expansion — Portfolio sorting and action review

The portfolio adds one optional filter for `resident-initiated`, `resident-help-offer`, `work-refusal`, and `social-mediation`, populated by current event projections. The default list still emphasizes actual active projects. Candidate actions are visually separated from accepted work orders and show the owner/source. A filter never sorts survivors by willingness or pressure. Search exposes action ID/source rather than private trait or trauma details.

The detail view gives the player three primary controls when supported: inspect owner facts, accept through the project/task owner, or dismiss/defer. An override appears only when the exact current owner command exists. After dispatch, the screen reports acceptance/refusal and the owner’s reason, returns focus to the project portfolio, and prevents a duplicate submit. If the current host cannot route the action, the row is marked informational and the UI does not render a fake button.

### Field 08 expansion — Fair workload, accessibility, and privacy

Content avoids making residents compete for recognition by accumulating the most projects. Voluntary help remains voluntary, and refusal does not turn a person into a story obstacle. The work board cannot display trauma/refusal reasons in a public task list when the source is sensitive; it may show a neutral “not available” state and reveal the reason only in a private detail view with authorization. Public notices name a survivor only through consent and an existing publication route.

Accessibility exposes the event type, source, available actions, and irreversible consequence in text. Focus order cannot place the override immediately before the safe decline control without a clear distinction. Audio cues follow the existing accessibility coordinator. Readers can dismiss all notification overlays and later find the owner event through the portfolio without reopening its original action.

### Field 09 expansion — Exact-once events, saves, and performance

Autonomy state and its 20 authored action templates stay in SurvivorAutonomySystem; ideology state stays in IdeologicalFrictionEvents; project/construction state stays in the current build owner; worker assignments stay in roster/work owners; inventory remains canonical. The work portfolio stores only supported cross-reference identifiers. If an owner emits no stable identifier, implementation must stop before persisting a guessed link.

The deterministic acceptance profile runs the same seed and survivor state twice, checks that autonomy events/cooldowns match, and verifies no UI opening changes trigger order. It then saves after project acceptance, after a refusal, during a pending override, and after mediation. Restore must not replay a project start, double-apply an override consequence, or make a dismissed event visible again as new. Large resident populations use bounded event queries and listener disposal.

### Field 10 expansion — Integration tranche and review evidence

The first tranche tests one resident-initiated project through an existing host route, one refusal that the player honors, and one accepted mentoring/help interaction. The next tranche may add explicit override only after the current owner’s consequence and save behavior are fully observable. The ideology tranche proves one confrontation response and one urgent mediation path from their true thresholds, with the construction result independent.

Acceptance covers no project consumer, no material, invalid destination, duplicated event, owner refusal, voluntary help declined, work refusal honored, explicit override accepted/refused, construction cancellation, ideology threshold edges, conversion, schism, mediation, reload, inaccessible actions, private reason hidden from public view, and performance with many residents. The handoff lists exact host/source routes and unresolved seams. This turns public works from a player-only task list into a living community proposal process without adding parallel project, autonomy, roster, ideology, inventory, or save authority.
## Pass 36 — Research-to-water works readiness without a second water ledger

This pass connects public water projects to the integrated `ResearchUnlockBridge`, the existing deep-well and WaterTreatment owners, and the current Plan 189 source/intake boundary. It addresses a common civic-project fiction error: a blueprint, a source advisory, available liters, and safe treated water are different facts. The project board can explain the difference and offer a supported next action; it cannot create a water-source registry, reserve bulk liters, change source quality, or declare an aquifer safe. The Plan 189 authority map is the reference for source IDs and admission. A proposed civic job that needs an architecture change stops at the owner decision instead of embedding a parallel intake route in public-works content.

### Field 01 expansion — Keep four water facts independent

The public works card may project four facts when their owners answer: a technology is unlocked; a source is identified and not blocked; a built source is producing; and WaterTreatment has accepted and categorized the resulting liters. A fifth fact, potable delivery at a destination, requires the current water treatment and Fluid logistics owners to confirm it. These facts cannot be compressed into an “operational well” checkbox. A research breakthrough is not a constructed well; a producing deep well emits raw water into the treatment intake; an intake advisory can block a source; and a successful bulk-water treatment operation still does not prove that a particular community tap is reachable.

The portfolio stores only canonical project/task identifiers and owner-returned receipts. It does not keep the quantity of water produced or delivered. On refresh it asks the right owner again, displaying “unknown” if a route is not exposed. A failed query never becomes a zero-water observation, and an absent source never becomes a fictional dry aquifer.

### Field 02 expansion — Unlock-to-project compatibility matrix

| Research signal | Civic project use | Required live evidence | Prohibited inference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `unlock_water_advanced_filter` | Prepare a filtration work request | Research bridge result, canonical item/recipe consumer, required materials | Does not improve water until the accepted owner operation changes it |
| `unlock_water_purify_recipe` | Offer a workshop batch task | Recipe-unlocked query, inputs, craft receipt, WaterTreatment result | Does not add clean liters when the recipe is merely visible |
| `unlock_deep_well_hydraulics` | Review a deep-well installation request | Research capability, `DeepWellSystem` construction/operation state, power result | Does not create an intake, aquifer capacity, or limitless supply in civic data |
| Piezometer advisory for a canonical source | Decide whether to suspend or inspect a source task | `WaterTreatmentSystem.IsIntakeSourceBlocked` result and current producer receipt | Does not diagnose the whole settlement’s water or alter aquifer readings |
| Fluid network delivery | Confirm the tap reaches a destination | Existing endpoint and allocation result | Does not make a remote community connected by map proximity |

These are compatibility rows, not new modifiable catalog entries. The exact consuming API and visible route must be verified per row before it becomes an actionable button.

### Field 03 expansion — Public water-work record contract

The content proposal uses a compact view model with a project reference, source reference, current owner status, last owner receipt, player-facing action candidates, and a provenance line. It has no mutable `stored_liters`, `quality_override`, `aquifer_rating`, `delivered_to_village`, or private maintenance clock. A project may reference a documented synthetic source only if the water authority map accepts the identifier and its admission semantics are explicit; a creative location name is not a valid source ID.

The contract supports three safe states: `OBSERVED` when an owner returned a current fact; `ACTIONABLE` when an existing route accepts a command; and `UNAVAILABLE` when the consumer route or supporting evidence is missing. A fourth UI label, `AWAITING_OWNER_RESULT`, describes an accepted operation with no final receipt yet. None of these states advances a project on its own. The civic project owner remains responsible for proposal, work scheduling, acceptance, cancellation, and completion.

### Field 04 expansion — Storyline: The Tap With Two Ledgers

At a settlement meeting, three residents disagree over whether the shared tap is “fixed.” One person remembers a completed pump; another has seen a treatment warning; a third lives at the far end of the distribution route. The player inspects the project record. Research shows the advanced filter breakthrough is unlocked, but the item has not been made. The well owner reports a pump built and producing raw intake. The piezometer advisory marks the canonical source blocked today. WaterTreatment refuses the source; Fluid has no new delivery receipt.

The player can publish a careful public notice, organize an inspection through the relevant owner if its command exists, or defer a celebratory opening. An attempted opening cannot overrule the intake gate. The next chapter records an accepted test after the advisory changes, then follows the batch through treatment and an actual destination allocation. The residents still debate maintenance and access, but their disagreement is grounded in distinct receipts instead of contradictory UI totals. The story closes when the public notice names what is running, what remains blocked, and where water has actually arrived.

### Field 05 expansion — Side-quest bank with owner gates

**The Empty Filter Crate** checks the research bridge, recipe consumer, required inputs, craft result, and canonical inventory receipt. It may conclude as a procurement plan if no item is produced. **The Well Is Not a Tap** follows the raw-water source into treatment and then Fluid delivery; each absent handoff leaves the quest in an honest staging outcome. **The Marker at the Headworks** compares a displayed source label against the piezometer catalog and refuses hand-authored IDs. **A Notice Before the Ribbon** lets the player delay a public claim without penalizing project trust. **The Night Shift Valve** exposes an existing route-allocation or valve command only if its owner can accept it. **A Repair Party Without a Forecast** can finish a physical work order while a source advisory is pending, as long as the construction owner accepts that scope.

**Two Families, One Queue** asks the player to inspect a real delivery receipt and disclose allocation limitations; it cannot mint water or reorder sinks. **The Red Tag** lets residents place a narrative closure notice on a proposed task only after the project owner returns a valid closure state. **The Intake That Came Back** refreshes a previously blocked owner result and proves that opening the civic board neither lifts nor re-applies the block. Each quest’s conclusion stores only existing owner receipts and narrative completion through the campaign/quest authority.

### Field 06 expansion — Source advisory and build state must not race

The Plan 189 map says the water-treatment intake gate is the admission point and that producers must name an accepted source ID. The public-works sequence therefore queries source status at the operation boundary rather than relying on yesterday’s report. A well can be built but blocked; an advisory can change between proposal and tick; a construction request may still be safely accepted while source intake remains blocked. Civic UI makes those distinctions visible and never tells a player that a project completion bypasses the owner gate.

The public project lifecycle remains transactional: submit through the current project/work owner, observe its acceptance or rejection, and render only the returned result. If the water system has no public query for the detail a card wants, the card is read-only and the plan records the missing read seam as a foreman decision. Do not infer it by parsing a save file or duplicating the owner’s state.

### Field 07 expansion — Resident initiative attaches to a public water work item

The integrated survivor-autonomy owner can emit resident-initiated project proposals, help offers, and refusals. The project portfolio may attach such an event to a water task only when the event includes a stable project reference and the current work owner accepts it. It can show “offer to help inspect the valve” without assigning a role, moving inventory, or enrolling the survivor in an unsafe field action. An explicit refusal remains a social fact; the player cannot convert it into consent to sample water or enter a hazard area through the work-override seam.

Ideological mediation may change whether a public meeting reaches a compromise, while the source and delivery facts remain unchanged. A neutral mediator’s response does not satisfy a construction dependency. The two outputs receive separate receipts and the public record describes both without blending them into a success score.

### Field 08 expansion — Community-facing UX and accessibility

The project panel labels evidence by owner in concise language: “research unlocked,” “well installed,” “source currently blocked,” “raw water accepted,” “treated water present,” and “destination receipt confirmed.” The detail sheet expands each label with a time/source reference when one is returned. It includes a one-click route only if the host has a truthful receiving panel. A disabled action explains the missing owner response in one sentence; it does not name a speculative resource requirement.

Keyboard focus moves from current status to provenance, supported next actions, and public wording. A long list of destinations uses a filter and lazy detail lookup, not repeated whole-world scans. The public-facing notice is previewed before publication and distinguishes technical state from social confidence. A high-contrast symbol accompanies every water-quality term so color is never the sole signal. All cues use the integrated audio coordinator and honor mute/reduced-audio preferences.

### Field 09 expansion — Persistence and query budget

Project save ownership does not change. The new projection does not require a public-works water save section. After reload, the view re-fetches source admission, production, treatment, and delivery from their owners; a saved task cross-reference cannot become proof that a source is operating. Historical notices may quote archived owner receipts if the campaign journal supports source/time capture. If that archival contract is absent, the notice is visibly current-state text and is not presented as historical evidence.

The board makes one grouped projection request for the selected project and caches the result only for the panel lifetime. Changing project selection invalidates that view cache. Updates are event-driven when current owner seams provide them; otherwise a bounded refresh occurs on explicit user action or ordinary screen refresh. No per-frame query, per-survivor source scan, or cross-settlement loop is permitted. Save/reload acceptance proves that the canonical owners restore independently and the project UI does not duplicate water totals.

### Field 10 expansion — Pilot and acceptance gates

Pilot one supported settlement, one mapped source, one research unlock, and one existing production path. First show research unlocked with no built facility; then show a built deep well with no valid power or active operation; then show source-advisory refusal; finally show an accepted raw-water intake, treatment result, and real downstream allocation if the current host exposes all four. An explicit “not supported by host route” branch is acceptable and must block promotion of that action to a playable button.

Acceptance covers missing and malformed source IDs, source blocked before proposal, block changing after proposal, absent blueprint, blueprint but no materials, constructed but inactive well, owner receipt missing, raw/treated type mismatch, no destination endpoint, closed valve, stale historical notice, duplicate submission, failed save restore, and a large settlement list. A reviewer traces every number to a sole owner and confirms no new liters, quality state, source registry, or save section exists. Promotion also needs a host route, current project acceptance, Plan 189 conformance, truthful feedback, and focused verification selected by the integrator. This pass turns water works into a legible civic chain while respecting the single bulk-water owner and the source-admission contract.
### Pass 36 supplemental public-water project docket — 24 task cards

The following content records exercise the water-work chain without creating an independent source or volume simulation. A record may become actionable only where its current receiving owner exposes a command. All delivery and treatment claims require a returned owner receipt.

| Candidate ID | Civic request | Evidence and end state |

| water_repair_cancel | A construction task is canceled after materials are prepared. | Construction/inventory owners resolve the returned materials; public works creates no refund ledger. |

| water_rain_proposal | A neighborhood suggests a rain collection project. | Require a documented producer/source contract before adding a playable water output. |
| water_tank_label | A tank has an unclear public label. | Update authored notice only after its canonical inventory/structure owner validates the identifier. |

## Pass 36 supplemental public wording and decision states

The public notice uses short statements that fit common project surfaces: “Research is complete; installation is not recorded.” “The source is currently blocked at intake.” “Raw water reached treatment; no delivery receipt is available.” “Water was allocated to the listed destination.” Each line carries the owner/time reference when available. Writers must not collapse them into “the district has clean water” unless every necessary owner has proved that larger claim.

A work order may be technically complete while a wider civic objective remains unresolved. The maintenance handoff can still record a successful physical repair if the construction owner accepted it, even when source admission is blocked. This enables meaningful progress without falsifying service availability or holding unrelated residents responsible for a technical dependency.
## Pass 36 worked sequence — The Common Tap from blueprint to destination

The sequence follows one civic request across research, construction, source admission, treatment, distribution, and public wording. It is a chain of independent owner receipts rather than a campaign-owned water simulation.

1. Residents propose repairing the shared tap. The civic project owner accepts the proposal and returns a stable project reference. Without that result, the project board stores no active work order.
2. The player sees that the advanced filter recipe is researched. This status comes from ResearchUnlockBridge and is shown as a capability only.
3. The crafting owner reports that one required input is missing. The player postpones the batch or opens a supported supply route; no filter item is synthesized.
4. The deep-well capability is unlocked. DeepWellSystem reports that the pump is not installed. The board marks installation as a separate work dependency.
5. The construction owner accepts an installation proposal and returns its own task receipt. Public works does not set the deep-well built flag.
6. After construction, the deep-well owner reports installation. Power and operation are checked through their owners before production is described.
7. The producer attempts a raw-water intake under its canonical source ID. The Plan 189 piezometer advisory currently blocks that source, so WaterTreatment refuses admission.
8. The project screen leaves the physical installation complete and water service unresolved. It does not roll back the build, bypass the gate, or claim the aquifer is empty.
9. A later owner refresh reports that intake is no longer blocked. At the next real producer operation, WaterTreatment returns the raw-water receipt.
10. The player submits a filter craft through the current recipe owner. Canonical inventory reports the produced item; only an accepted treatment action can then change the appropriate water state.
11. The treatment owner returns a result with its actual WaterType/amount. The project card renders exactly that source result without rounding away type or provenance.
12. Fluid logistics reports that one endpoint received an allocation. Other settlements remain unserved unless their own endpoint and allocation receipts exist.
13. The civic notice names the repaired installation, the intake condition, the treatment result, and the destination receipt as separate dated facts.
14. A resident offers to help publish the notice. SurvivorAutonomySystem supplies the offer and the project owner accepts or refuses its publication task.
15. On reload, the project, deep well, water treatment, piezometer, Fluid, and inventory states restore through their current save owners. The story does not replay a craft or an intake.

The same sequence has useful partial endings: proposal accepted but build rejected; installation complete but power absent; intake blocked; raw water accepted but treatment unavailable; treatment complete but no destination connected; and a destination served while another remains outside the network. This gives the public works campaign several honest outcomes without collapsing a system chain into one boolean.
## Pass 37 — Regional mutual aid under territory and supply-line pressure

This pass expands public works from individual projects to regional coordination by composing TerritoryControlSystem, ColonySystem, OutpostSettlementSystem, CommunicationsSystem, SeasonalCelebrationSystem, AudioAccessibilityCoordinator, and existing reputation/archive owners. A settlement, outpost, supply corridor, garrison, or broadcast can support a public-work story, but none is a new civic ledger. Territory controls territory; colonies own their supplies/buildings; public works owns only its project proposal and accepted handoff.

### Field 01 expansion — Corridor eligibility

TerritoryControlSystem owns canonical faction holdings, fortification levels, garrisons, supply corridors, contests, raids, restoration, and throughput. Public works can request a corridor projection for a project that needs materials or a safe approach. It cannot calculate a new territorial boundary, assign faction control, or treat a project vote as a contest resolution.

The project card labels CORRIDOR_ACTIVE, CORRIDOR_DISRUPTED, LOCATION_CONTESTED, and NO_TERRITORY_RESULT. A disrupted corridor may delay a work order if the project owner accepts that dependency. It does not automatically cancel construction or change public trust. A restoration operation remains a territory-owner action.

### Field 02 expansion — Colony and outpost support

ColonySystem and OutpostSettlementSystem each own their own forward positions, capacity, garrison, supply, consumption, condition, risk, and save state. Public works may select a canonical colony/outpost as a project site or materials relay. It does not merge colony supplies with shelter inventory or create a regional stockpile.

A project requiring an outpost can ask for a supply receipt, a garrison/route condition, and a construction acceptance. If the outpost is starving or overrun, the project shows the returned blocker. A field clinic, watchtower, depot, or relay building is named only when the colony owner reports it; definitions alone do not create a public service.

### Field 03 expansion — Mutual-aid request contract

The regional request record contains project ID, origin, destination, canonical material IDs, requested owner action, dependency references, and public wording. It contains no faction standing, corridor liters, colony food, or duplicate work progress. The receiving owner returns accepted, rejected, delayed, or unavailable.

Requests are visible to residents as bounded proposals. The player can prioritize, defer, publish, or withdraw through current project controls. A territory result can influence the explanation but cannot be overwritten by a public vote. A communication result can notify a partner, but acknowledgment is not delivery until the receiving owner proves it.

### Field 04 expansion — Supply disruption and graceful degradation

When a corridor is raided or a colony line is disrupted, the project plan recomputes only the dependent tasks. It may keep local preparation, surveying, or documentation active. It does not invent replacement supplies or assume the player can cross hostile territory. If a current owner supports an alternative corridor or outpost, the player can choose it; otherwise the project waits.

Graceful degradation is a feature: “material request sent,” “route disrupted,” “local work continues,” and “destination unavailable” are all valid states. The public record explains the dependency without blaming a named faction unless TerritoryControlSystem supplies that fact. The UI avoids a percentage that combines territory, construction, and public confidence.

### Field 05 expansion — Storyline: The Road Between Three Wells

Three settlements ask for a shared water repair. The shelter can provide a research blueprint but not the entire material set. A canonical supply line connects the first settlement to an outpost depot; TerritoryControlSystem reports that the corridor is active. ColonySystem confirms the depot and a watchtower, while OutpostSettlementSystem reports limited supplies.

The player authorizes a regional request. CommunicationsSystem sends the proposal to the two communities. A raid disrupts the corridor before the materials arrive. The player continues local survey work, asks the territory owner for restoration if supported, or reroutes through a second canonical outpost. One settlement holds a seasonal harvest observance while waiting, using SeasonalCelebrationSystem’s real resource and participant rules; the celebration does not count as construction.

The final chapter records either a delivered material receipt, an accepted reroute, or a transparent delay. Archive and reputation owners receive only the accepted public event. The community learns that cooperation can survive a broken corridor without pretending the road never closed.

### Field 06 expansion — Communication and public notice

CommunicationsSystem supplies range, antenna, frequency, jamming, and delivery state. Public works uses it for proposal relay, progress notice, and return-message receipt. It does not store a second inbox or make every resident a recipient. A notice can be drafted offline and transmitted later when an owner route allows it.

Public wording distinguishes “sent,” “received,” “acknowledged,” “materials dispatched,” and “materials delivered.” A faction’s radio silence is not treated as refusal unless the communications and diplomacy/project owners return that result. Private negotiation details remain out of the public record unless a publication command permits them.

### Field 07 expansion — Celebration and work boundaries

SeasonalCelebrationSystem owns holidays, anniversaries, resource expenditure, participants, tradition streak, morale multiplier, memorable celebration, and skipped-holiday penalties. Public works can schedule an authored notice or community meeting around a returned holiday date. It cannot create an annual civic calendar, award morale directly, or turn a festival into a completed project.

An anniversary may commemorate a prior completed work only when the archive/project owner provides the milestone. A skipped celebration can remain a human story beat, but the system’s penalty is applied only by SeasonalCelebrationSystem. Public works reports the celebration receipt separately from construction progress and material movement.

### Field 08 expansion — Audio and emergency readability

A disrupted corridor may generate an existing raid, radio, or low-power cue. AudioAccessibilityCoordinator owns visual notifications, ducking, coalescing, and reduced-stimulation modes. Public works adds no duplicate siren or “project failure” sound. A text-only player sees the same route blocker, source, and next supported action.

Long regional boards use icons plus labels for active, disrupted, contested, and delivered. Focus returns to the selected project after a notice arrives. The board remains usable during a celebration or emergency overlay, and closing it removes event listeners. High-severity notifications are not drowned by repeated supply updates.

### Field 09 expansion — Archive, reputation, and deterministic handoff

ShelterArchiveSystem records a project decision, regional delivery, milestone, discovery, or memorial only through its owner. Shelter reputation or territory evidence changes only when the relevant accepted event reaches the current owner. Public works stores stable references and public text, not a second reputation, faction, or archive history.

The same seed and owner state yield the same corridor projection, supply result, celebration eligibility, and project order. Save/reload cannot deliver materials twice, count a celebration twice, or repeat a territory restoration. Old saves with missing outpost/corridor IDs render historical references as unavailable. Bounded queries cover many colonies, corridors, projects, and public notices.

### Field 10 expansion — Regional tranche and release gates

The tranche starts with two canonical settlements, one outpost depot, one active corridor, one disrupted corridor, one communications relay, one seasonal event, and one accepted public-work project. It proves independent owner receipts and a useful partial path. The second tranche adds territory restoration only if its current host route is callable.

Promotion requires no duplicate inventory, colony, outpost, territory, celebration, communication, reputation, or archive authority. Negative cases include overrun outpost, starving colony, contested location, missing endpoint, jammed frequency, skipped holiday, canceled project, and reloaded delivery. The player must always know whether a project is locally progressing, waiting on a corridor, or completed at the destination.

## Pass 38 — Skilled stewards, shelter renovation, and regional work quality

This pass expands civic projects through SurvivorEducationSystem, HobbySystem, ShelterExpansionSystem, ShelterArchiveSystem, SeasonalCelebrationSystem, and the existing project/construction owner. It gives public works deeper labor stories and visible craftsmanship while keeping structural stability, room condition, knowledge, mastery, resources, and saves in their current systems.

### Field 01 expansion — Work eligibility from education and hobby owners

EducationSystem may return a skill unlock or graduation result. HobbySystem may return a mastery tier or facility-gated session. Public works uses those results to filter eligible proposals or offer optional assistance; it does not assign a worker or translate a hobby tier into an engineering statistic.

A resident can be a trained observer, apprentice, craftsperson, or unassigned volunteer. Work owner and roster/autonomy owner decide whether they actually participate. A refusal remains a social event. No civic score is derived from how many residents have high mastery.

### Field 02 expansion — ShelterExpansionSystem boundaries

ShelterExpansionSystem owns spatial grid, collision, labor investment, structural stability, excavation penalties, alerts, reinforcement, room condition, renovations, depth shafts, and persistence. Public works may reference a shelter renovation or a community-facing room project if that owner returns it. It cannot create a second stability value or declare a civic building complete from a story scene.

Cards distinguish proposal, accepted project, labor invested, completed expansion, stability warning, reinforced, and renovated. A celebration can commemorate completion only after the owner receipt. An education or hobby facility requirement may be checked through its owner, not guessed from a room name.

### Field 03 expansion — Storyline: The Schoolroom Under the Beam

A community requests a schoolroom and public workshop in a deeper shelter level. EducationSystem reports that a schoolroom facility would provide its existing bonus if available; HobbySystem reports a craft session requirement. ShelterExpansionSystem rejects the first placement because of a spatial collision and warns that excavation stability is low.

The player chooses a smaller renovation, commissions a reinforcement through the shelter owner, or postpones the room. A resident offers to teach masonry; the education/hobby and work owners validate the offer separately. When the room is eventually renovated, the schoolroom and workshop facts become visible, but no student graduates or craft mastery changes until their daily owners tick. The story rewards patience and structural honesty.

### Field 04 expansion — Labor investment and public accounting

The project card reports labor investment from the construction owner, materials from inventory, and structural condition from ShelterExpansionSystem. Public works can publish a receipt or request additional labor but cannot spend resources on preview. If a project is canceled, the owner decides refund and partial progress behavior.

A resident work refusal can reduce available labor only where the work owner accepts it. An autonomy help offer can increase eligible assistance only through a supported action. A mediation outcome can make the meeting smoother but cannot add labor or stability.

### Field 05 expansion — Regional material and route dependency

A renovation may depend on a colony depot or territory corridor. ColonySystem and TerritoryControlSystem return delivery and access state. Public works displays those dependencies without merging stock. A blocked route leaves local design/inspection work available where the project owner permits it.

The board identifies which material is locally available, requested, delivered, or consumed. It never turns a public notice into inventory. A repeated reload cannot deliver the same building material twice.

### Field 06 expansion — Celebrations and milestones

SeasonalCelebrationSystem owns holidays, anniversaries, scale, costs, participation, streaks, memories, and skipped penalties. A completed renovation can be commemorated as a milestone if ShelterArchive or the celebration owner accepts it. The celebration does not increase structural stability, education skill, or project completion.

Authors supply small, medium, and large variants only when the celebration owner returns the scale and resources. A low-power or shortage result can reduce the available celebration choice while leaving the work receipt intact.

### Field 07 expansion — Archive, press, and trust

ShelterArchiveSystem records decisions, milestones, discoveries, and achievements. The existing press engine may generate a deterministic print result where its route exists; the public works plan does not assume the targeted source call site is already wired. A printed notice is not a project completion unless the project owner returns it.

Shelter reputation changes only through its current owner. A truthful report may say “renovation paused by stability warning” even when a public audience is disappointed. The story avoids a local trust meter and uses returned evidence.

### Field 08 expansion — Accessibility and quiet work

Construction warnings, low power, celebration, and route messages use AudioAccessibilityCoordinator’s existing visual/text behavior. A stability warning is never sound-only. The project panel places current structural status, owner action, materials, labor, and public wording in focus order.

Large project lists use compact cards and lazy detail. Controller back returns to the project portfolio without canceling work. Reduced-stimulation mode suppresses repeated noncritical notices while keeping an explicit stability blocker visible.

### Field 09 expansion — Save and performance

ShelterExpansionSystem, education, hobby, colony, territory, celebration, archive, inventory, press, and project owners save independently. Public works stores references and public text. Reload must not reapply labor, reinforcement, celebration cost, archive entry, or material delivery.

Performance coverage includes many rooms, projects, learners, hobby sessions, regional dependencies, archive entries, and public notices. The panel queries selected project detail, not every room and every resident on each frame.

### Field 10 expansion — Stewardship tranche

The first tranche includes one renovation collision, one stability warning, one accepted reinforcement, one education/hobby eligibility result, one regional material dependency, one celebration variant, one archive milestone, and one refusal. Promotion requires exact owner receipts and clear partial outcomes.

Public works becomes a long-term stewardship loop: residents learn, craft, repair, celebrate, document, and sometimes postpone. The mechanics stay truthful because each effect remains with its owner.

## Pass 39 — Civic service desk, maintenance recurrence, and high-volume requests

This pass defines a civic service desk for many public requests, inspections, repairs, and maintenance returns. It composes project/construction, ShelterExpansionSystem, ColonySystem, TerritoryControlSystem, inventory, archive, reputation, communication, celebration, autonomy, and audio owners. It does not introduce a civic currency, a trust score, or a parallel maintenance ledger.

### Field 01 expansion — Request taxonomy

Requests are typed as new project, repair, inspection, delivery, public notice, maintenance return, mediation, or archive lookup. The request owner returns accepted, rejected, pending, complete, canceled, or unavailable. A request type is content metadata, not a new state authority.

The service desk lists source, destination, owner, dependencies, privacy, and next action. A resident request can be public or private. The board does not expose a private refusal reason in a public queue.

### Field 02 expansion — Recurrence without a second calendar

Maintenance returns use an existing owner’s condition or project result. If no owner exposes a recurrence schedule, the service desk can create a reminder/quest request but cannot tick a maintenance timer. SeasonalCelebrationSystem supplies only holiday/anniversary timing; it is not a maintenance calendar.

A completed work may generate an owner-returned follow-up. The service desk stores a reference and displays due/unknown only when the owner supplies it. Opening the desk never advances a day.

### Field 03 expansion — Infrastructure facts

ShelterExpansionSystem returns room condition, stability, renovation, reinforcement, and depth. Colony/outpost owners return site condition, buildings, supply, garrison, and risk. Territory returns access and corridor state. Public works composes them without a regional condition score.

A project can be physically complete while a maintenance return remains open. The UI names those separately. A public celebration can mark completion, but not maintenance.

### Field 04 expansion — Resource and inventory custody

Inventory is checked at operation time. A request can preview materials, but only the accepted construction, crafting, colony, or inventory owner consumes them. Canceled work returns whatever the owner’s contract says; public works does not assume a refund.

The desk never reserves a resource when a resident submits a suggestion. Competing requests are resolved by their owners. A “materials requested” label is not “materials delivered.”

### Field 05 expansion — Territory and delivery dependencies

TerritoryControlSystem returns active/disrupted/contested corridor state. ColonySystem and OutpostSettlementSystem return delivery/supply results. A project can continue local design or inspection while a remote delivery waits. The service desk does not invent a local substitute.

Access changes refresh dependent requests at submit time. A route closed after a preview produces a clear blocker. A restored corridor creates a new owner result rather than replaying old delivery.

### Field 06 expansion — Resident agency and mediation

Autonomy events can create project proposals, help offers, refusals, or social mediation. IdeologicalFrictionEvents owns confrontation, conversion, schism, and urgent mediation. The service desk links those events to a project only through stable IDs.

A help offer does not assign a job. A refusal does not delete a request. A mediation result does not add materials, labor, or public reputation. A private reason remains private.

### Field 07 expansion — Public record and press

ShelterArchiveSystem receives accepted decisions, milestones, discoveries, and achievements. The press engine may print a deterministic result where its host route exists; absent route remains a draft. Public works uses owner-backed facts and never creates a publication queue as a second authority.

Notice templates include request submitted, route delayed, work accepted, work complete, maintenance due, maintenance unknown, and work canceled. The source and date appear when provided.

### Field 08 expansion — Dense-board accessibility

The desk supports filters by owner, destination, status, privacy, dependency, and age. It shows a total, focused row, reason, and supported action in text. AudioAccessibilityCoordinator supplies any critical alert cue; ordinary request updates remain readable without sound.

Keyboard/controller navigation supports bulk dismissal of view notices but not bulk cancellation of gameplay work. A player can open a detail, return to the same row, and preserve the current filter.

### Field 09 expansion — Save, migration, and performance

Public works saves only its accepted project/request references through current quest/project owners. Condition, supplies, territory, colony, construction, inventory, archive, and celebration remain separate. Reload cannot reapply work or delivery.

The load profile contains 250 requests, 30 projects, 12 destinations, 10 corridors, 80 archive entries, 40 residents, and 20 notifications. Metadata loads first; owner detail is selected. A migration with missing IDs preserves an unavailable historical row.

### Field 10 expansion — Service-desk promotion

The tranche requires one request of every type, one private refusal, one route disruption, one maintenance return, one archive record, one publication draft, one celebration link, one save/reload, and one duplicate-submit guard. No new service currency or trust score is accepted.

The service desk succeeds when it helps the player decide what to do next while preserving the authority that actually changes the world.
